The AI model has generated a borderline prediction set that includes two possible categories, one of which aligns with imaging features typical of a meningioma. Because the system evaluates a single imaging slice it cannot assess growth rate, tumour location or histological grade, all of which are essential to distinguish entities that may appear similar on MRI [ncbi-meningioma-statpearls]. Meningioma is a common primary brain tumour that may be discovered incidentally or may cause neurological deficits according to size, location, growth characteristics and grade [ncbi-meningioma-statpearls][nci-meningioma][who-cns5]. The overlap in appearance between different tumour types and between low-grade and higher-grade meningiomas makes confident separation difficult from a solitary study [ncbi-meningioma-statpearls].

It is therefore appropriate to discuss the findings with a neurosurgical or neurological specialist, who may consider a dedicated contrast-enhanced MRI, a thorough clinical and neurological examination and, where indicated, histological sampling to determine grade and inform management [nci-meningioma][ncbi-meningioma-statpearls]. Management options range from observation with serial imaging to surgical or radiation-based approaches, selected after comprehensive evaluation of location, symptoms, growth and overall condition [nci-meningioma][icom-meningioma-consensus]. Ongoing specialist review and interval imaging are recommended to monitor growth and to reassess if new or progressive neurological symptoms develop [nci-meningioma][icom-meningioma-consensus].
